subject: Equinor hosting discovery — VPC / air-gap constraints (recap & actions)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@equinor.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@equinor.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Equinor hosting discovery — VPC / air-gap constraints (recap & actions)

Hi Samir / Priya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap so we’re aligned and to make next steps explicit. I’ve bolded items where we need confirmation from your side.

Summary of constraints you shared
- Data residency: all PII and telemetry (customer records + model logs) must remain in EU (Norway/Oslo region preferred).
- No general internet egress from inference hosts. Outbound traffic must be routed through customer-managed NAT/proxy with static egress IPs.
- Air-gapped option required for a subset of workloads: fully isolated compute with manual artifact sync for model weight updates.
- Key management: FIPS 140-2 / HSM-backed KMS is required for private deployments; no third-party KMS that requires outbound calls to non-EU endpoints.
- Audit & attestation: SOC 2 + penetration test report will be needed; annual evidence requested by security.
- Ops & connectivity: preferred connectivity is private peering (Direct Connect/ExpressRoute-equivalent). VPN as fallback during pilot is acceptable but must support stable MTU and traffic selectors.

Primary goals for the pilot
1) Validate low-latency inference within your VPC for core search ranking pipeline (target p95 latency < 150ms for a 128-token call).
2) Prove model update workflow for air-gapped pipeline: operator triggers model artifact sync, validates hash, and flips traffic.
3) Demonstrate auditability: log collection, retention policy, and proof-of-delivery for requests (no PII leakage).

Open questions / clarifications (action items for Equinor)
- Please confirm the target Oslo AZ(s) and whether a DR region (e.g., Stockholm) should be included in the pilot. (Samir)
- Can you provide the static outbound IP list / NAT egress appliance details for allowlisting? We need these for our control-plane/peering configuration. (Priya)
- Confirm whether your security team requires full air-gap for training pipelines as well, or only inference-serving.

Redwood proposed next steps (owners & ETA)
- Mina: Share a lightweight network sketch + preliminary IP ranges we’ll need to open on our side — by EOD today. (attached)
- Laura (Solutions): Schedule a 90-minute tech deep-dive with your netsec + infra teams to walk the proposed peering and offline sync process — propose Fri 10/2 or Mon 10/5.
- Aditya (Sales Eng): Draft a pilot scope & price estimate (30-day POC) and initial MOU to reflect E2E responsibilities — deliver by 10/4.

Attachments included: equinor-network-sketch.pdf (diagram + minimal ask list), redwood-mou-draft.docx (POC framing).

If that looks right I’ll book the deep-dive for Fri 10/2 09:00 CET (proposed) and loop in our Solutions Architect. Please reply with any edits to the action items above.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Equinor hosting discovery — VPC / air-gap constraints (recap & actions)

Thanks Mina — solid recap. A few quick confirmations and clarifying requests: 

1) Confirmed: Oslo primary, Stockholm for DR — we’ll include both in scope.
2) Outbound IPs: we’ll extract a short-list from our netops and share by EOD Thursday (10/1).
3) KMS: we have an HSM-backed KMS in Oslo; however, we need to validate if Redwood’s control-plane needs to make any outbound calls to a KMS endpoint — that will be a blocker for air-gap. Can you clarify whether your control-plane must call customer KMS during normal inference?
4) Cost & pilot: we’re interested in a 30-day POC but need a rough estimate before procurement can commit. Aditya, if you can mark price as indicative that helps speed sign-off.

Looping Priya for netops and procurement. Happy to take the tech deep-dive Friday if your team can do CET morning.

—Samir
Samir Khan
Cloud Security Lead, Equinor
samir.khan@equinor.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@equinor.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@equinor.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T18:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Equinor hosting discovery — VPC / air-gap constraints (recap & actions)

Samir — thanks, quick answers inline: 

> 3) KMS: we have an HSM-backed KMS in Oslo; however, we need to validate if Redwood’s control-plane needs to make any outbound calls to a KMS endpoint — that will be a blocker for air-gap. Can you clarify whether your control-plane must call customer KMS during normal inference?

Short answer: For our private deployment model we can operate in two modes:
- Fully offline (air-gapped) mode: Redwood ships a private control-plane appliance into your VPC (or we deploy a customer-managed control-plane) and uses an operator-driven flow to rotate keys and load model artifacts — no outbound KMS calls required.
- Connected private mode (preferred for faster ops): our control-plane (in EU region) can call into a customer KMS endpoint for envelope key wrapping, but we only do this if allowed and the endpoint is reachable; we can also support a proxy/relay inside your VPC to avoid egress from your private subnets.

So if your security team will not permit any outbound KMS calls from the control-plane, we should scope the pilot as the air-gapped operator-managed control-plane. If outbound is allowed via a proxy, we can use the connected flow for faster rollouts.

Preliminary IP ranges we will need opened (for the connected-flow or initial validation):
- 52.23.178.0/24 (control-plane staging)
- 18.205.32.0/24 (health checks/agent updates)
- 3.210.44.0/24 (S3-compatible artifact endpoint)

Those are initial placeholders — we’ll finalize after the tech deep-dive.

Next steps:
- I’ll attach the annotated network sketch (attached) and book the Fri 10/2 09:00 CET deep-dive unless you ask to move it.
- Aditya will put together an indicative POC price range by Monday 10/4.

If you want immediate privacy/policy language to share with security, I can send a short one-page whitepaper describing the air-gapped operator flow and KMS options.

Best,
Mina

Attachments referenced: equinor-network-sketch.pdf
